findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine fail to reach the minimum required temperature for sanitizing (160F) during today’s inspection. The dish machine appears to complete the wash step and fail to complete the rinse step, which is the high-temperature step of the process. The PIC was made aware of the issue and has requested service on the machine. In the meantime, staff are placing dishes from the dish machine into a triple sink basin of quaternary ammonia sanitizer. A follow-up will be conducted on September 14, 2026 to ensure the dish machine has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant to the left of the dish machine to be damaged and soiled. Ensure this sealant is repaired or replaced to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Light was observed passing through the gap beneath the exit door in the dinning area.The inspector advised the person-in-charge (PIC) to use a weather stripping to seal the gap so as to prevent entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following non food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Dust accumulation was observed on the fan covers in both walk-in coolers.
2. Soil accumulation (icy shade) was observed beneath the fan casing in the walk-in coolers by the dish self.

The inspector instructed the PIC to have the fan covers and fan casing cleaned to sight and touch so as to prevent contamination of foods stored in the walk-in cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two separate storage order violations in the walk-in cooler. Raw pork was stored in a bin with deli meat, and cooked chicken was stored in a bin with raw chicken. The PIC was informed and the contaminated items were discarded. Inspector conducted education while onsite regarding storage order. The cooler does have a storage order flyer posted. Ensure staff are supervising volunteers during food storage to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed cutlery and dining trays to be stored with their food-contact surfaces face-up with no adequate coverings. PIC was informed that the food-contact surfaces of items need to be covered or inverted to protect from cross-contamination. All items were inverted during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed mops to be stored with their mop heads on the floor. The PIC was informed that mops need to be stored such that they can safely drip dry to prevent bacterial accumulation and cross-contamination. All mops were properly inverted during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: Inspector observed four pans of eggs cooling in the walk in covered with pan lids. The lids were turned so that the heat can escape. The pan lids were twisted and pans separated. Ensure to develop a good habit and use proper cooling techniques. 

(A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: Inspector observes doors from the outside into the facility have gaps and cracks. The pest control company has had this on their list of client responsibilities. The PCO is doing service every two weeks. Follow all directions from the pest control company to completely eliminate pests. 

(A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13:  Inspector showed manager several areas where the base cove has holes, gaps and or broken or missing tile. Repiar these areas and ensure that they are maintained sealed. This will help in the control of pests. 

(A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Sliced deli meats are observed in the walk in #2. Deli meats are not date marked. Ensure that all foods taken in are properly date marked. The items were received yesterday. The packages were properly date marked today. The violation is considered corrected on site. 


3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).
